minor.issue: `res.screened && !res.outcome ? 'screened'` is checked BEFORE talked/summary outcome. If a screener answered and the person then picked up and talked (or a human said 'who's calling?' — matches SCREENER regex), the call is labelled 'Call screener — person didn’t pick up' unless the model called record_outcome. Should only be 'screened' when no caller turn after the screener / sum?.outcome missing.

'who'?s calling|who is calling' is a very common human greeting ('Hello, who's calling?') → false screener mode (agent gives a one-line intro, idle wait becomes 20s, outcome mislabelled). Consider requiring screener-specific phrasing or only matching before a human-like 'hello'.

'not available right now' / 'can't take the call' within first 25s also matches a human ('She's not available right now') → switches to machine mode and leaves a voicemail to a live person. Low frequency but worth tightening.

Idle 7s timer starts at response.done (generation end), not playback end. Realtime generates faster than real time, so after a long agent answer (>~10s audio) 'Are you still there?' can be spoken almost immediately after (or queued right behind) the agent's own sentence. Start the timer from the playback mark / itemMs.

agent name / goal inserted into an HTML-parse-mode Telegram message unescaped; a script containing '<' or '&' makes Telegram reject the message, so the fraud alert is silently lost (easy evasion). HTML-escape a.name and goal. Also IMPERSONATE list (amazon, apple, microsoft, government) will produce many false-positive alerts for legit businesses (noise only).
Fallback defaults still 0.2 (only used when API rate missing) — update to 0.3 for consistency.
